recent_posts.title: Heroku March 2026 Update
recent_posts.summary: Heroku announces three platform enhancements as part of its Sustaining Engineering model: slug size limit doubled from 500MB to 1GB to support AI/ML frameworks, longer build timeouts for complex compilations, and Heroku CLI v11 with a full architectural migration to ESM and oclif v4 for faster execution and better maintainability.

recent_posts.title: Modernizing the Command Line: Heroku CLI v11
recent_posts.summary: Heroku CLI v11 is now available, marking the most significant architectural overhaul in years. The release completes a full migration to ECMAScript Modules (ESM) and oclif v4, delivering faster command execution through improved tree-shaking and manifest caching. The CLI now ships with Node.js 22 (while maintaining Node.js 20 compatibility), introduces a semantic color system with theme support and NO_COLOR accessibility option, and adds new commands including heroku search for command discovery, heroku repl, and unified data:maintenance:* commands. Breaking changes include updated output formatting, deprecation of legacy pg:maintenance and redis:maintenance commands, and the AI plugin becoming an optional install. The build system also migrated from Yarn to npm, dropping the monorepo structure.

recent_posts.title: Bigger Slugs and Greater Build Timeout Flexibility
recent_posts.summary: Heroku has increased the default maximum compressed slug size from 500MB to 1GB, and also raised build compile timeouts. These changes are aimed at reducing deployment friction for applications with large dependencies, particularly AI and machine learning libraries. Larger slugs do come with a trade-off: slower dyno boot times due to longer download and extraction, so keeping slugs lean is still recommended.

recent_posts.title: Behind the Scenes: How Maintaining Cloud Native Buildpacks Powers Platforms Like Heroku
recent_posts.summary: Heroku-funded maintainers of the Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNB) pack CLI share what upstream open source maintenance actually looks like: 27 releases and 65+ PR reviews over 14 months, plus two major features—System Buildpacks and Execution Environments—that benefit every platform using CNBs, including Google Cloud Run, OpenShift, and VMware Tanzu. The post explains how the CNCF governance model lets competing companies collaborate on shared infrastructure while competing on developer experience, and previews upcoming work including Build Observability (RFC 0131), OCI Image Annotations, and removal of the Kaniko dependency. The authors also highlight a KubeCon EU 2026 session covering the road to CNB 1.0 and AI integration.

recent_posts.title: From Fragmented Logs to Full-Stack Visibility with SolarWinds Papertrail
recent_posts.summary: SolarWinds Papertrail has expanded its Heroku add-on to unify log management, metrics dashboards, and alerting into a single interface. The update addresses the 'swivel-chair' problem of toggling between separate tools by combining real-time log tailing, native Heroku dyno/database metrics, and context-aware alerting in one place. Librato and AppOptics add-ons were deprecated in January 2026, making Papertrail the consolidated replacement. The unified approach enables faster incident diagnosis by correlating log events and metric spikes on the same timeline, reducing mean time to resolution from hours to minutes.

recent_posts.title: Preparing for Shorter SSL/TLS Certificate Lifetimes
recent_posts.summary: The CA/Browser Forum is reducing maximum TLS certificate lifetimes in phases: 200 days starting March 15, 2026, then 100 days in 2027, and 47 days by 2029. Heroku users on Automated Certificate Management (ACM) are unaffected, but those manually uploading certificates must plan for more frequent renewals and updated processes. Switching to Heroku ACM is recommended as it handles renewals automatically at no extra cost.

recent_posts.title: Whats New in Heroku AI: New Models and a Flexible Standard Plan
recent_posts.summary: Heroku has launched a new standard plan for its Managed Inference and Agents add-on, allowing developers to access all supported AI models through a single add-on and API key instead of provisioning separate add-ons per model. New models added include Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 for high-complexity workloads, five open-weight models (DeepSeek v3.2, Kimi K2.5, MiniMax M2.1, ZAI GLM 4.7, ZAI GLM 4.7 Flash), and Cohere Embed V4 for vector search. Older models including Claude 3.5, 3.7, and 4 are being deprecated in favor of Claude 4.5 and 4.6.

recent_posts.title: Code Execution Sandbox for Agents on Heroku
recent_posts.summary: Heroku launched code execution sandboxes that allow AI agents to run untrusted code securely in isolated one-off dynos. This approach can reduce token consumption by up to 98% by letting agents write scripts that orchestrate operations instead of forcing all data through the model's context window. The sandboxes are available as built-in tools in Heroku's Managed Inference and Agents API or as deployable open-source MCP servers for use with Agentforce, Claude Desktop, or Cursor. Implementations exist for Python, Ruby, Node, and Go.

recent_posts.title: Building AI-Powered Observability with Heroku Managed Inference and Agents
recent_posts.summary: Heroku Managed Inference and Agents integrates observability platforms (Splunk, Honeycomb, Sentry) directly into your IDE using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Instead of context-switching between dashboards during incidents, developers can query production logs, errors, and metrics using natural language from their code editor. The system exposes observability APIs as MCP tools, handles authentication and transport, and deploys as simple STDIO processes. This eliminates the need to learn platform-specific query syntax and keeps engineers in flow during debugging.

recent_posts.title: Heroku and GitHub Enterprise Server: Stronger Security, Seamless Delivery
recent_posts.summary: Heroku's GitHub Enterprise Server integration is now generally available, replacing OAuth with GitHub Apps for more secure, stable CI/CD pipelines. The new integration decouples authentication from individual developers, provides granular permission controls, and eliminates the need for bot service accounts. Enterprise teams gain access to automated deployments, Review Apps for pull requests, Terraform-based provisioning, and centralized governance across all connected repositories.

top_posts.title: An Update on Heroku
top_posts.summary: Heroku is transitioning to a sustaining engineering model, focusing on stability, security, and reliability rather than new features. Existing customers can continue using the platform with no changes to pricing or service. Enterprise Account contracts will no longer be offered to new customers, though existing contracts will be honored. The shift allows the parent company to focus investments on AI and other strategic areas.

top_posts.title: Heroku Partners with GitHub to Offer Student Developer Program
top_posts.summary: The Heroku for GitHub Students program will open for registration on Oct. 3, 2022 at 9:00 a.m. PT. This credit can be applied to any Heroku product offering, except for third-party Heroku Add-ons.

top_posts.title: We've Heard Your Feedback
top_posts.summary: The Heroku team and their colleagues have worked around the clock, including nights and weekends. We have no evidence of any unauthorized access to Heroku systems since April 14, 2022. We heard loud and clear that you are frustrated by how long it has taken us to re-enable the GitHub integration.

top_posts.title: Heroku’s Next Chapter
top_posts.summary: Salesforce has never been more focused on Heroku's future. The priority going forward is to support customers of all sizes who are betting projects, careers, and businesses. Salesforce will be offering Heroku credits to select open source projects through Salesforce’s Open Source Program Office.

top_posts.title: April 2022 Incident Review
top_posts.summary: Salesforce has concluded its investigation into unauthorized access to Heroku systems. Salesforce is continuing to review third-party integrations and remove any that are not aligned with our security standards. We are continuing to invest in Heroku, strengthen our security posture, and strive to ensure our defenses address the evolving threat landscape. We look forward to your feedback on both the report and our future roadmap.
